findings.name: Montana Disabled Veteran (MDV) Property Tax Assistance Program
findings.description: Montana reduces the property tax rate on a primary residence for veterans with a 100% service-connected disability (or their unmarried surviving spouse), on a sliding scale of 50% to 100% reduction based on income and filing status. For tax year 2026, single filers with federal adjusted gross income under $62,598 qualify (100% reduction up to $48,152, phasing down to 50% at $57,782-$62,598); married/head-of-household filers qualify under $72,229 (100% reduction up to $57,781, phasing down to 50% at $67,413-$72,229); unmarried surviving spouses qualify under $54,573 (100% reduction up to $40,127, phasing down to 50% at $49,759-$54,573). The homeowner must own or be under contract to purchase the home and occupy it as a primary residence at least 7 months per year. Applications are due April 15 (late applications considered for the following year).
findings.value: Property tax rate reduced 50%-100% depending on income tier and filing status
otherReqs: 100% disability rating from a service-connected injury per VA letter
Own or be under contract to purchase the home; occupy as primary residence at least 7 months per year
Income limits apply (2026: single <$62,598; married/HOH <$72,229; unmarried surviving spouse <$54,573)
Application due April 15
findings.form: Montana Disabled Veteran Property Tax Relief Application (MDV)
findings.sourceExcerpt: The veteran must have 100% disability from an injury related to service. Reductions range from 50% to 100% based on income level and filing status. Apply by April 15.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate Fee Waiver
findings.description: Montana waives the veterans' cemetery fee and all motor vehicle registration fees for two non-commercial vehicles for veterans who are Purple Heart recipients with a 50% or more service-connected disability rating (cemetery fee not waived for this category), or who have a 100% VA disability rating (or are paid at the 100% disabled rate for a service-connected disability). The Disabled Veteran plate also authorizes disabled parking privileges. A letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs stating the disability rating or payment status is required, and applicants apply through their local county treasurer.
findings.value: Registration fee and veterans' cemetery fee waived for two non-commercial vehicles
otherReqs: Purple Heart recipients need 50%+ service-connected disability rating (cemetery fee not waived for this tier)
100% VA disability rating (or 100% disabled pay rate) qualifies for full waiver including cemetery fee
Vehicles must be non-commercial
Apply through local county treasurer
findings.agency: Montana Motor Vehicle Division / County Treasurer
documentation: Letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs stating disability rating or payment status
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans who meet one of the following requirements are eligible for fee waivers: Purple Heart recipients who have a 50% or more service-connected disability rating from the VA, or a 100% disability rating from the VA or payment at the 100% disabled rate for a service-connected disability. A person eligible for the waiver is exempt from the veterans' cemetery fee for two sets of special veteran license plates and all motor vehicle registration fees imposed for two motor vehicles that are not used for commercial purposes.

findings.name: Combat-Disabled Veteran Half-Price Deer/Antelope License
findings.description: Montana veterans with certain combat-connected injuries may qualify for half-priced deer and antelope hunting licenses. Up to 50 such licenses are issued annually. Applicants must submit the annual Combat Disabled Application and contact Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks Licensing to confirm which combat-connected injuries qualify.
findings.value: 50% discount on deer and antelope hunting licenses (limited to 50 licenses annually)
otherReqs: Must have a qualifying combat-connected injury (specific criteria confirmed by FWP Licensing)
Limited to 50 licenses issued per year
Combat Disabled Application form required
findings.sourceExcerpt: A veteran with certain combat-connected injuries may be entitled to half-priced licenses for deer and antelope. Up to 50 licenses will be issued annually.

findings.name: VA Hospital Patient Free Fishing / Purple Heart Conservation License
findings.description: Veterans who are current patients at a VA hospital may fish in Montana without a license, provided they carry documentation signed by VA hospital staff confirming their patient status. Separately, residents and nonresidents who have been awarded a Purple Heart, regardless of age, may fish and hunt upland game birds with a Conservation License issued by Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks upon verification of the Purple Heart award and DD-214.
findings.value: Free fishing for VA hospital patients; free upland-bird hunting/fishing Conservation License for Purple Heart recipients
otherReqs: VA hospital patients must carry documentation signed by VA hospital staff confirming current patient status
Purple Heart recipients must provide Purple Heart verification and DD-214
documentation: VA hospital patient documentation, or Purple Heart award verification and DD-214
findings.sourceExcerpt: Residents and nonresidents who have been awarded a Purple Heart, regardless of age, may fish and hunt upland game birds with a Conservation License issued by FWP. Verification of Purple Heart and DD 214 Form required to qualify. Veterans who are patients at a VA Hospital can fish without a license in Montana.

findings.name: Honorably Discharged Veteran Tuition Waiver
findings.description: The Montana University System waives remaining in-state tuition (as a last-dollar award, after all other financial aid is applied) for honorably discharged veterans who are Montana residents attending a qualifying MUS campus. The veteran must have received an Honorable discharge (Honorable Under General Conditions is not accepted) for active duty service other than for training purposes, must have elected to become eligible for VA education benefits under Title 38 or Title 10 but had those benefits expire or become exhausted, must apply no later than the third week of the first semester, and must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress. The waiver does not cover flat fees and applies to both undergraduate and graduate students.
findings.value: Last-dollar waiver of remaining in-state tuition after other aid is applied
otherReqs: Honorable discharge for active duty service other than training
VA Title 38/Title 10 education benefits must be expired or exhausted
Apply no later than the third week of the first semester
Must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress per campus SAP policy
documentation: Proof VA education benefits are expired/exhausted
findings.sourceExcerpt: A resident of the State of Montana attending a qualifying MUS campus who has received an Honorable discharge (Honorable Under General Conditions will not be accepted) for active duty service beyond training, and who elected to become eligible for V.A. education benefits under Title 38, or Title 10, with benefits now expired or exhausted... Operates as a LAST DOLLAR award, covering only the remaining tuition balance after all grants and scholarships are applied.

findings.name: Veterans' Employment Preference (State Hiring)
findings.description: Under MCA 39-29-102, when a Montana public employer uses a scored hiring procedure, an applicant must have added to their score 5 percentage points if a veteran, or 10 percentage points if a disabled veteran or eligible relative (a disabled veteran cannot stack both). The applicant must still meet the position's minimum qualifications to receive the points. When a public employer uses a non-scored selection procedure, preference is given, in order, to disabled veterans, persons with disabilities, veterans, eligible relatives, and eligible spouses over any nonpreferred applicant with substantially equal qualifications.
findings.value: 5 percentage-point score preference for veterans; 10 percentage-point preference for disabled veterans/eligible relatives
otherReqs: Applicant must meet the position's minimum qualifications to receive preference points
Disabled veteran preference (10 points) and veteran preference (5 points) cannot be combined
documentation: DD-214 or proof of veteran/disabled veteran status
findings.sourceExcerpt: 5 percentage points if the applicant is a veteran... 10 percentage points if the applicant is a disabled veteran or an eligible relative. A disabled veteran who receives 10 percentage points under subsection (1)(b) may not receive an additional 5 percentage points under subsection (1)(a).

findings.name: Montana State Veterans Homes
findings.description: Montana operates three state veterans nursing homes — in Columbia Falls (Montana Veterans' Home, 105 intermediate/skilled-care beds plus 12 domiciliary beds, including a 15-bed Alzheimer's unit), Butte, and Glendive. The Columbia Falls home is Medicare/Medicaid and VA certified and is directed by the Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services, an executive agency of state government. The Columbia Falls facility has served veterans since 1896.
findings.value: Skilled nursing and domiciliary care at three state-operated veterans homes
otherReqs: Medicare/Medicaid and VA certification requirements apply
Specific admission criteria set by DPHHS, not detailed on the summary page fetched this session
